state.request: Recommend CanLang's first emitted application format for workerd, choosing between JavaScript and WebAssembly. Adoption takes precedence in the user's search for the strongest result. Keep the implementation language of the compiler separate from the executable application output under discussion. This is a request for guidance, not code changes. A target's popularity or an abstract performance argument does not establish suitability.
state.language: The intended language is a concise DSL authored by AI for business SaaS built around CRUD, access rules, workflows and Cloudflare's managed infrastructure. Its native capabilities include D1, R2, Durable Objects, Queues and email. Canonical authorization and operation schemas serve both MCP and server-rendered daisyUI/HTMX interfaces, alongside inline locale messages. Required behavior includes exact 64-bit int and decimal/money values, deterministic type/effect analysis, durable results and inline BDD examples. Application authors cannot bypass the DSL through unrestricted general-purpose code. V1 excludes substantial media, design and observability engines. At present, the repository supplies 44 application-design sources and a syntax parser; it supplies no semantic compiler, executing runtime or execution benchmarks.
state.primary_evidence: According to Cloudflare's documentation, V8 executes both JavaScript and Wasm in Workers (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/web-standards/). Cloudflare's supported Rust/Wasm deployment produces a JS entrypoint, connects platform facilities with wasm-bindgen glue, and converts Rust futures into JS promises (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/languages/rust/#how-this-deployment-works). Managed-service access is therefore feasible through Wasm. Workers provides Wasm SIMD and excludes threading; additional runtime code commonly accompanies Wasm output and may affect package size or startup. WASI remains partially supported and experimental (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/webassembly/). A portable computation core and existing Rust/C libraries are potential Wasm uses, while Cloudflare-specific services require host-side connections. These observations do not establish a performance winner for CanLang.
state.correctness: Values passed into D1 use JavaScript representations. Although SQLite INTEGER has signed 64-bit range, D1 does not accept BigInt bindings and JS Number represents integers safely only within its safe-integer limit (https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/#type-conversion). Consequently, either executable target requires a codec that preserves exact values in storage and on the wire. Treating all int/decimal/money calculations as ordinary Number arithmetic would violate the language. Application permissions, transaction semantics, schema types and BDD behavior follow neither from Wasm validation nor from running JS. Those duties belong to CanLang's checker and common operation runtime, applied before and around the generated effects.
state.tradeoffs: Direct access to the platform's native APIs and conventional asynchronous request handling are advantages of JS output. Human-readable generated code and source maps may help debugging; a dynamic JS representation does not transfer static CanLang analysis away from its compiler. A Wasm backend provides a reusable binary computation core, native fixed-width arithmetic and access to SIMD or existing libraries. Maintaining it also entails the application generator/toolchain and the boundaries for host calls, objects, strings and asynchronous work. With a hybrid, JS owns handlers, bindings and rendering, while a Wasm module supplies computation; that arrangement requires two artifact formats and an explicit connecting contract. Existing CanLang workloads have not shown a computation bottleneck warranting such a split. JS still requires accurate scalar helpers and adapters for managed services, so reducing host boundaries does not eliminate runtime implementation. Without CanLang measurements, expected size, performance and adoption outcomes for any option remain unverified hypotheses.
state.scope: The initial design should commit to one canonical application target. It should not add application-specific backend selection, an authored build manifest, an anticipatory second backend, a deployment wrapper or another DSL primitive. Generated SQL, platform binding requirements, HTML/CSS/assets and BDD artifacts remain necessary companion outputs, separate from the executable target decision. For an initial runnable increment, execute existing CRUD and one guarded operation on workerd, render the server UI, expose that same operation through MCP, and run its inline examples. Reject unsupported declarations with explicit diagnostics instead of silently discarding them to claim a running draft. This proposed implementation increment has not been delivered. Later, concrete evidence about a library or workload could support an internal Wasm helper while retaining one SaaS authoring path.

target.instructions: For the described CanLang workload, which first emitted application format most effectively balances adoption and simplicity with faithful semantics and plausible platform support? Evaluate each candidate's specific advantages and implementation burdens. The target label itself supplies no assurance of performance, protection or correct behavior.

criteria.javascript: Generate JavaScript ES modules consumed by workerd, backed by a single versioned common runtime and exact scalar/storage helpers. Prioritize straightforward async and managed-service access with inspectable output, while retaining the compiler/runtime responsibilities and postponing a portable Wasm computation core.
criteria.wasm: Generate the application's Wasm core together with a JS entrypoint and host-facing interfaces. Prioritize portability of the binary core, fixed-width arithmetic and reuse of existing libraries, while taking on toolchain/glue upkeep and Cloudflare integration despite having no demonstrated performance gain for this workload.
criteria.hybrid: Adopt JS request handlers and runtime together with a Wasm module for computation from the outset. Seek native host integration plus compiled calculations and library reuse, while carrying both artifact formats, their boundary and coordinated build before CanLang has shown a computational requirement for them.
criteria.unresolved: Leave the initial target undecided because the provided runtime evidence and application requirements are insufficient to justify an implementation direction without additional findings.
